ai.literal: Divisions being well-structured, injury not fearing, victorious army, king's wealth among all, is foremost.
ai.translation: An army that is complete in all its divisions and fears no wounds is the foremost among all the treasures of a king.
ai.modern: அனைத்து உறுப்புகளும் நிறைந்து, போர்க்களத்துத் துன்பங்களுக்கு அஞ்சாமல் வெற்றிபெறும் படை, ஒரு அரசனுடைய செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet opens the chapter on the excellence of the army. The word 'uṟuppu' refers to the traditional fourfold divisions of an ancient army: chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry. The poet states that a victorious army must not only be structurally complete ('uṟuppamaintu') but also courageous enough to face wounds and death without fear ('ūṟañcā'). Such an army is described as the 'talai' (foremost) among all the 'veṟukkai' (wealth or treasures) that a king can possess.

ai.literal: At the time of ruin, injury-not-fearing courage, at the time of defeat, to the ancient army except, is rare.
ai.translation: The courage that fears no wounds in times of ruin is rare for any but an ancient, time-tested army in times of defeat.
ai.modern: அழிவு வரும் காலத்தில் காயங்களுக்கு அஞ்சாத வீரமும், தோல்வி ஏற்படும் காலத்தில் தளராத மன உறுதியும் பழமையான படைக்கு அல்லாமல் வேறு யாருக்கும் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the unique quality of a seasoned, traditional army. It states that when ruin or defeat is imminent, the steadfast courage that does not fear wounds or suffering is extremely rare to find in any force other than such an ancient, time-tested army. The key words 'உலைவிடம்' and 'தொலைவிடம்' refer to critical moments of distress and defeat, while 'வன்கண்' represents the unyielding fortitude required to withstand them.

ai.literal: If they roar, what is the use, an ocean-like army of rats? When a cobra breathes, they will perish.
ai.translation: Of what use is an army of rats, even if it roars like the ocean? They will all perish the moment a single cobra merely breathes.
ai.modern: கடல் போல ஆரவாரம் செய்தாலும் எலிகளின் பகைப்படை என்ன செய்ய முடியும்? ஒரு நாகப்பாம்பு மூச்சுவிட்டால் அவை அனைத்தும் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates that a vast army of weak and cowardly soldiers is useless against a single, powerful hero. The poet compares a large but weak army to a roaring ocean of rats. No matter how much noise they make, they cannot withstand a true warrior, symbolized by a cobra. The mere hiss or breath of the cobra is enough to scatter and destroy the entire host of rats.

ai.literal: Without defeat, not succumbing to betrayal, being of traditional lineage, fortitude, that indeed is an army.
ai.translation: A true army is one that possesses traditional fortitude, remaining undefeated and immune to the enemy's subversion.
ai.modern: தோல்வி அடையாமலும், பகைவரின் சதிக்கு ஆளாகாமலும், பாரம்பரியமாகத் தொடர்ந்து வரும் மனவலிமையைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே உண்மையான படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of a true army. It highlights that real military strength lies in 'vaṉkaṇ' (fortitude or valor) that has been passed down through generations of tradition ('vaḻivanta'). This courage must remain undefeated ('aḻiviṉṟi') in battle and must be completely resistant to the enemy's attempts at subversion or betrayal ('aṟaipōkātu'). The poet emphasizes that an army's true worth is determined by its historical resilience and unyielding loyalty rather than mere numbers.

ai.literal: Even if the god of death, having raged, comes against [them], standing united in opposition—that strength indeed is an army.
ai.translation: Even if the God of Death himself should advance in a rage, a true army is that which stands united and resists him.
ai.modern: எமனே சினந்து எதிர்த்து வந்தாலும், ஒன்று கூடி எதிர்த்து நிற்கும் வலிமையைப் பெற்றிருப்பதே உண்மையான படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate courage and solidarity of a true army. Even if the god of death (கூற்று) rages (உடன்று) and marches against them, the soldiers must not scatter in panic. Instead, they must band together (கூடி) and stand firm in resistance (எதிர் நிற்கும்). The collective strength (ஆற்றல்) to face even the absolute certainty of death is what truly constitutes an army (படை).

ai.literal: Valor and honor, excellent path-following, and trustworthiness—thus these four indeed are protection for the army.
ai.translation: Valor, honor, following the noble path of tradition, and trustworthiness—these four are the true safeguards of an army.
ai.modern: வீரம், மானம், முன்னோர் காட்டிய நல்வழியில் நடத்தல், மற்றும் நம்பிக்கைக்குரிய தன்மை ஆகிய இந்த நான்குமே ஒரு படைக்குப் பாதுகாப்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential qualities that protect and sustain an army. First is 'மறம்' (valor or bravery in battle) and second is 'மானம்' (honor, which prevents soldiers from retreating in disgrace). Third is 'வழிச்செலவு', which refers to following the disciplined, noble traditions of warfare established by ancestors. Fourth is 'தேற்றம்', meaning trustworthiness or reliability, which ensures loyalty to the leadership. Together, these moral and behavioral traits form the ultimate defense (ஏமம்) of an army, far exceeding mere physical strength.

ai.literal: Withstanding the vanguard, that which advances is the army, having known the method of withstanding the battle that has come upon them.
ai.translation: A true army is that which, knowing the strategic methods of withstanding an imminent battle, successfully resists the enemy's vanguard and advances.
ai.modern: தனக்கு நேர்ந்த போரை எதிர்கொள்ளும் முறையை அறிந்து, பகைவரின் முன்வரிசைத் தாக்குதலைத் தாங்கி முன்னேறிச் செல்வதே சிறந்த படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential quality of a true army. A real army is not merely a crowd of soldiers, but a disciplined force that understands the tactical methods of resisting an imminent battle. Armed with this strategic knowledge, it is capable of withstanding the fierce onslaught of the enemy's vanguard and steadily advancing. The word 'தார்' specifically refers to the enemy's front line, and 'தன்மை' denotes the tactical expertise required to counter them.

ai.literal: Even though fighting spirit and strength are absent, an army will obtain greatness by its imposing military appearance.
ai.translation: Even if it lacks active fighting spirit and physical strength, an army can still win glory through its imposing appearance and orderly array.
ai.modern: போரிடும் தன்மையும் வலிமையும் இல்லை என்றாலும், ஒரு படை தனது அணிவகுப்பின் கம்பீரத்தினால் பெருமை பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the psychological value of a disciplined and well-organized military force. Even if the soldiers temporarily lack active fighting spirit (அடல்தகை) or physical strength (ஆற்றல்), the sheer sight of a grand, orderly battle-array (படைத்தகை) can command respect and deter enemies. The word 'தகை' in 'படைத்தகை' refers to the imposing appearance, dignity, and traditional prestige of the army. Thus, structure, discipline, and visual majesty alone can sometimes win the day and bring glory (பாடு) to the state.

ai.literal: And meanness, and lingering discontent, and poverty, if they are absent, the army will conquer.
ai.translation: If an army is free from meanness, lingering discontent, and poverty, it will achieve victory.
ai.modern: சிறுமைக்குணம், நீங்காத வெறுப்பு, வறுமை ஆகியவை இல்லாதிருந்தால், அந்தப் படை வெற்றி பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three internal defects that can ruin an army, regardless of its size or weapons. First is 'ciṟumai' (meanness or smallness of spirit), which refers to a lack of courage or noble character. Second is 'cellāத் tuṉi' (lingering discontent or resentment), which represents internal discord or grievances against the ruler that do not go away. Third is 'vaṟumai' (poverty or deprivation), which saps the soldiers' strength and morale. If an army is free from these three flaws, it is guaranteed to win.

ai.literal: Even though an army possesses an abundance of steadfast soldiers, in the absence of commanders, it is nothing.
ai.translation: Even if an army has an abundance of steadfast and loyal soldiers, it will come to nothing in the absence of capable leaders.
ai.modern: நிலைத்து நிற்கும் வீரர்களை மிகுதியாகக் கொண்டிருந்தாலும், தகுதியான தலைவர்கள் இல்லாதபோது அந்தப் படை இல்லாமல் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that leadership is the most critical element of a military force. Even if an army consists of a vast number of steadfast, permanent, and loyal soldiers (nilaimakkaḷ), it cannot succeed without capable commanders (talaimakkaḷ) to lead them. The term 'nilaimakkaḷ' denotes seasoned, reliable troops who do not flee, while 'talaimakkaḷ' refers to the strategic leaders. Without these leaders to guide and coordinate, the strength of the soldiers is wasted, and the army ultimately fails to exist as an effective force.
